BiblicalUsage: This word for the mighty ones — strong men, bulls, champions — turns up in the songs and the prophets. Deborah sings of 'the pransings of their mighty ones' as the enemy horses flee; the psalm says man ate 'angels' food', the bread of the mighty; and Jeremiah hears 'the neighing of his strong ones' as the invader's horses approach from Dan.
TheologicalSignificance: The mighty ones of earth — the horsemen, the champions, the armies — are strong until God moves, and then their hooves break and their bread fails. I believe the contrast is deliberate: human might makes a fine song until it meets the Lord, and only His strength endures.
